protocol.description:
This protocol lets a shell component, such as the bar or the settings app, show and change the brightness of each wl_output. The compositor owns the brightness: it drives a laptop panel's backlight, an external monitor's own brightness over DDC/CI, or, when the display has neither, dims the output's picture itself. A client sees one level on one scale whatever the compositor uses behind it.
Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_output_brightness_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_output_brightness_v1 objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Brightness objects created through it are unaffected.

request.name: get_output

description.summary: control the brightness of an output

request.description: Create an object that reports and changes the brightness of output. The compositor sends control, then level, right after the object is created. Several objects may control the same output; each one gets the events that every change causes.

interface.name: crownos_output_brightness_v1
interface.description:
Reports and changes the brightness of one wl_output. The level is perceptual, from 0 to 10000: 10000 is the brightest, and equal steps look like equal changes to the user. Each control has a lowest level, which can be above 0, so that the display never goes fully dark.
If the wl_output goes away, the object becomes inert: the compositor sends no further events for it and ignores its requests, and the client should destroy it.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no backlight, no DDC/CI and no gamma: the level cannot be changed

entry.name: backlight
entry.summary: the backlight of a built-in panel

entry.name: ddc
entry.summary: the monitor's own brightness, over DDC/CI

entry.name: software
entry.summary: the compositor dims the output's picture

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. The compositor sends no further events for it.

request.name: set_level
request.description:
Change the brightness of the output to level, from 0 to 10000. A level above 10000 is an invalid_level protocol error.
The compositor raises a level below the lowest level of the control to that lowest level. Writes to slow hardware are coalesced: when several set_level requests arrive before the hardware has taken the previous one, the compositor writes only the newest. The compositor answers each accepted request with a level event that carries the clamped value.
When the control is none, the compositor ignores this request.

request.name: refresh

description.summary: read the brightness from the hardware again

request.description: Ask the compositor to read the brightness from the hardware again, for example after the user changed it with the monitor's own buttons. The compositor sends a level event if the level changed.

event.name: control

description.summary: how the compositor changes the brightness

event.description: How the compositor changes the brightness of this output. Sent first, right after the object is created, and again if the compositor finds a different control later, for example when a monitor starts to answer over DDC/CI. A client disables its brightness control while the control is none.

event.name: level
event.description: The brightness of the output, from 0 to 10000. Sent after every control event, so the client knows the initial state is complete once the first level arrives; after every accepted set_level with the clamped value; and whenever the level changes for any other reason, such as a brightness key, another client or a refresh. When the control is none, the level is 10000 and never changes.
